review_note: Keep the open-issues device, errata, research caveats, capstone requirements and final satirical close. Cut explanations of the course’s own honesty, remove unverified classroom predictions, and make the reading-limit and capstone instructions direct.

edits.before:
Three parts of the protocol are left out of scope on purpose. Each gets an
issue number, a reason, the reading where its documentation starts, and a
question you could take into your capstone.
edits.after:
Three parts of the protocol are left out of scope. Each gets an issue number,
a reason, the reading where its documentation starts, and a question you
could take into your capstone.
edits.reason: The list already shows that the omission is deliberate; remove the recurring announcement of intention.

edits.before:
questions the course isn't equipped to settle for you. That's the honest
reason, and the reason week 12 sketches rather than teaches.
edits.after: questions the course isn't equipped to settle for you.
edits.reason: The actual scope limitations are enough; remove the sentence certifying the course’s honesty.

edits.before:
Same destination. Different obstacle. And the obstacle already has two weeks
  of this course pointed at it.
edits.after: Same destination. Different obstacle.
edits.reason: Keep the compact comparison and let the next paragraph identify the earlier weeks.

edits.before:
Look at where that obstacle sends you. **Uncertainty** is what week 3 said an
envelope marks --- a place where the sender doesn't know the answer. It is what
week 9's rate limit is for --- moving when you can't predict the other person's
next step. OI-1 is a hard open issue, and it does not turn out to need
vocabulary this course hasn't already built. That is a better argument for how
the twelve weeks are arranged than anything the course could assert about
romance.
edits.after:
**Uncertainty** points back to week 3's envelope --- where the sender doesn't
know the answer --- and week 9's rate limit, for moving when you can't predict
the other person's next step. Those give you two places to start with OI-1.
edits.reason: Retain the useful connections without claiming the course has supplied all the vocabulary romance needs or praising its own structure.

edits.before:
**The course's reading of it.** Everything in weeks 1--11 can be used to
persuade. This course taught it so you could interoperate, and it's why the
Field Experiment's ethics reflection is graded, not an appendix.
edits.after:
**The course's reading of it.** The decoder reads an envelope; it also writes
one. The rate limit paces closeness; it can also pace a sale.
edits.reason: Use the deck’s existing concrete examples of persuasive use instead of announcing the course’s virtuous intention.

edits.before:
**And the reason the reflection carries marks.** Route two of the capstone
varies a protocol parameter on people who never agreed to be in a study. That
is not a flaw in the design; it *is* the design, and it is why the ethics
reflection is worth 35% rather than sitting in an appendix.
edits.after:
**And the reason the reflection carries marks.** Route two of the capstone
varies a protocol parameter on people who never agreed to be in a study. The
ethics reflection is worth 35%: you must account for what you do to them.
edits.reason: Keep the marked component and its concrete purpose without a defensive contrast or a second appendix refrain.

edits.before:
Thursday's lab reviews every proposed parameter against four questions, and
they are worth having in your head before you arrive:
edits.after: Thursday's lab reviews every proposed parameter against four questions:
edits.reason: The instruction to prepare is already clear from the named lab and checklist.

edits.before:
The first is the one students argue with, and the argument is worth having.
Garfinkel breached expectancies deliberately and learned a great deal doing it.
He was also studying strangers he would never meet again. You are varying a
parameter on your flatmate and your tutor, which is a different consent and a
different aftermath. "Less eye contact than usual" is inside the range of
ordinary behaviour. "None at all" is a breach, and a breach is Garfinkel's
method, not this course's.
edits.after:
Garfinkel's method deliberately breached expectancies. This experiment keeps
variations inside ordinary behaviour; you may be working with a flatmate or
tutor you will see again. "Less eye contact than usual" is inside the range of
ordinary behaviour. "None at all" is a breach, and a breach is Garfinkel's
method, not this course's.
edits.reason: Remove a predicted student argument and the unverified claim that Garfinkel studied only strangers he would never meet again. The existing eye-contact rule is retained and flagged for substantive review.

edits.before:
**One minute.** Hands up if your parameter failed a question. Failing it here
costs you nothing. Failing it on Thursday costs you a redesign.
edits.after:
**One minute.** Hands up if your parameter failed a question. Use the failed
question to revise it before Thursday.
edits.reason: Replace a rehearsed cost contrast with the next practical step.

edits.before:

"has drawn published criticism", which is precisely the sort of gesture a
specification should not be allowed to make. So, specifically: Moskowitz
published a comment in the same journal a year later. The objection is **not** that the proposal is false. It is that the
edits.after:
**The criticism.** Moskowitz published a comment in the same journal a year
later. The objection is **not** that the proposal is false. It is that the
edits.reason: Present the criticism without staging a correction of the previous paragraph, and do not call an abstract-based summary the criticism in full.

edits.before:
Read that as an engineer and it is the best-formed known issue on this entire
reading list. It names the claim. It says exactly what the current evidence can
and cannot distinguish. It specifies the test that would close it. And it was
published next to the thing it criticises, under a name, where anyone can find
it.
edits.after:
The comment gives us a format for an erratum: name the claim, say what the
evidence cannot distinguish, and specify the test that would close it.
edits.reason: Keep the usable format; remove the superlative and the explanation of why the reader should admire it.

edits.before: The register is not finished and was never meant to be.
edits.reason: The E-6 activity itself invites additions to the register.

edits.before:

edits.after:
If you can't find a claim to file against, look at the "the course's own
observation" line at the foot of each week's research review. Each is a

edits.reason: Keep the fallback route without announcing that the course anticipated this exercise.

edits.before:

leans on them, and that is exactly why they are on the list.

edits.before:

edits.reason: The preceding instruction now makes the capstone connection directly.

Each open issue's entry point, with what it cannot tell you. The second column

edits.after: Each entry pairs a reading with its limit.

edits.before:
One model belongs on that table and isn't on it. Petty and Cacioppo's
elaboration likelihood model is the standard entry point for persuasion, and
this course could not retrieve a text to check it against, so it is not cited.
That is the rule the course has applied to itself all semester, applied one
last time where it costs something.
edits.after:
Petty and Cacioppo's elaboration likelihood model is a standard entry point
for persuasion. We could not retrieve a text to check it against, so it is
not cited here.
edits.reason: Keep the missing-source record without a performance of how costly it was to apply the citation rule.

edits.before:
If you take a single habit out of these twelve weeks, make it the second
column: find out what a source cannot tell you before you quote what it can.
edits.after: Before using a source in your capstone, check what it does not establish.
edits.reason: Make the source-use instruction concrete and remove the incorrect column reference and graduation-style sign-off.

edits.before:
There is a version of this material that ends with *pass as one of them*. It
would have been easier to write and easier to mark, and it is the outcome this
course was built to refuse.
edits.after:
There is a version of this material that ends with *pass as one of them*.
That is not this course's outcome.
edits.reason: Preserve the course’s refusal without an unverifiable claim about how easy the alternative would have been to write and mark.

edits.reason: Do not assign every student a history of corrective programmes, clinics or relatives.
